A motion was adopted that this report be accepted and that the temporary
recorder be instructed to cast one ballot for the election of the permanent officers

the permanent officers had been elected. President Parsons assumed the chair
at 3:00 P.M. and called the convention to order. He delivered the following
opening remarks to the Convention.
Brothers, I thank you for your expression of confidence in me, and I wiU
attempt to meastire up to the responsibilities you have placed upon me.
I herewith wish to welcome particularly those Alimini Delegates who are
here to represent their respective Chapter Alumni Organizations, as well as all
the other Alumni who have come to attend the Convention because they are inter
ested in its procedures. We certainly need to build the interest of our Alumni
in our Fraternity, and we appreciate the interest you are hereby indicating by
your presence here.

Each one of you Undergraduate Delegates, as well as the official Alumni
Delegates, are the elected representatives to this Convention which actually is
the Government of Psi Upsilon. While attending this Convention, therefore, you
have serious obligations to carry out and among these, are:

A. To ascertain the current conditions of the Chapters of our Fraternity.
B. To receive and analyze the report of the Executive Council and its
staff as to the results of the legislation passed at the last Convention.
C. To secure full reports from your fuU time staff, and where you find
unsatisfactory conditions, to consider and recommend remedies where such
are required.

D. To consider the recommendations of the Executive Council as to
needed legislation and to pass such resolutions as you find you can support.
E. To carry back to your respective Organizations a full report of the
proceedings here and to explain the important actions of this Convention.
You understand that it is within your powers to recommend such resolutions
to this Convention which you consider wise, although the objects of such may not
be recommended to you by the Executive Council.

You should be sure that the reports you receive are fully imderstood by you
and that they are in sufficient detail to give you the information you desire.

I would say you should concern yourselves with the problems of our Chapters
which are not operating in conformance with "Psi Upsilon Chapter Standards" in
order to promulgate such legislation as you feel necessary to correct these matters.
Perhaps you should even request members of such Chapters to make a report to
you as to just what the problems are of such Chapters in this respect.

Page Four

While I am sure that Brother Fretz of our full time staff will report to you,
it may be that you will wish to ask him a of in order to
variety questions fully
acquaint yourselves with the different phases of our Fraternity, and if so, you
should have him explain such matters so that you fully understand them.

If you have any questions which you would like to direct to the Executive
Council, please feel free to do so, for I am sure its members will be glad to answer
your questions fuUy.

As the President of the Executive Council, I can report to you that our
Chapter's financial matters need improvement, that new systems of issuing bills,
receiving payments thereon, and paying our debts are a great need of the hour for
Psi Upsilon.

I can say to you that a number of our Chapters need new systems of rushing
starting with a better concept of just what type of material they seek and then use
effective methods and procedures to carry out a successful rush.

I personally believe we are making progress, and I believe that Earl Fretz
deserves your eternal thanks for the service that he has rendered to us. In most
cases, I believe his knowledge of Fraternity management has been greatly appre
ciated, for he has been able to assist a number of our Chapters during the year in
connection with a variety of special problems which have risen.

I am, heartened with an increasing display of Alumni interest, and I
believe, if
we could find the necessary manpower we seek for our full time staff, we could
move much faster in the goals we are
seeking relative to our Fraternity operations.
I hope that each of you will point out to us any possible candidates for staff
assistance whether he be a man to aid in Alumni work, a younger man to relieve
Brother Fretz of much of the editorial work on the "Diamond", or still another
man to aid in Chapter calls and
problems that such visits uncover. Some young
Alumnus with magazine or newspaper experience might very well be delighted to
take on the major responsibilities relative to the publishing of our "Diamond" on
a part time basis for which we stand ready to
recompense him on a reasonable
basis.

The finances of the Executive CoimcU, as you will learn, still leave much
to be desired. Our budget is not balanced, and we have been unable to raise
the general level of our Alumni dues. We are determined, however, to carry out
our program as instructed by the last two Conventions and secure, as soon as we

can, the necessary manpower even if the result is a larger deficit.

While our scholarship has improved considerably over the course of the
last year, we still have a long way to go before we would be a welcomed addition
to a campus where we do not presently have a Chapter. We intend to spend
considerable time on this in the next year and hope to have a far better picture
to present to you relative to it next summer.

As you will ascertain from the Council Communication, the fortunes of the
Omega Chapter have improved considerably, and this is most heartening to me,
although the crucial test of its resurgence in operations will come in the year
ahead. You will hear more of the problems of our Iota Chapter which have
concerned us seriously, and we are indeed fortunate that we have a number of
its Alumni actively pursuing a planned program to bring the operations of this
Chapter in line with the Fraternity's requirements.
So the welfare of the Fraternity is your business. You should ascertain the
facts and legislate the remedies. It is up to you to demand performance on the
part of all our Units so that each operates on a high plane and in conformance

Page Five

with your mandates. If you settle for anything less, you will fail in your ap
pointed responsibilities, and this, I am sure, you will avoid.

practice be continued in the future.

RESOLVED: That this Convention endorses the program undertaken
by the Psi Upsilon Foundation under the provisions of which Foundation
funds can be used for academic assistance to members and chapters in ways
other than the direct grants to individual undergraduates.

RESOLVED : That the Convention put on record that it acknowledges
the outstanding improvement of the Omega chapter and compliments the fine
work of undergraduates and graduates for the rebuilding of the Omega
chapter.
RESOLVED: That this Convention goes on record as reaffirming the
existing legislation regarding hazing that was passed at previous Psi UpsOon
Conventions. This Convention further directs the Executive Council and its
staff to devote time and effort to enforcing the existing laws. If, and when
hazing occurs, evidence of such must be brought to the immediate attention
of the Executive Council and the ensuing Convention for appropriate action.
RESOLVED: That this Convention hereby prohibits any undergraduate
member, who is on either academic or individual social prohationary status,
from holding chapter office during the term of this probation.
